proposed_fix.description: Confirm where the ~200ms delay on inbound emailservice calls originates (pod/node resources, network path, or an injected delay) and apply only reversible, human-approved mitigations such as a pod restart or rescheduling.
steps: Compare emailservice pod and node CPU, memory, throttling and network metrics for the onset window against baseline to find a resource or network cause.
Check for recent changes affecting emailservice (deployments, config, sidecar or service-mesh fault or delay rules, network policies) and review them.
Inspect inbound-call spans (caller to emailservice) to see whether time is spent in the network, a proxy/sidecar, or queueing before the handler.
If a delay-injection rule or recent config change is found, revert it after human approval.
If no config cause is found and the pod or node looks unhealthy, restart one emailservice pod (gated on approval and on remaining replicas serving), and watch latency-50/90 for recovery.
If the node is implicated, cordon it and reschedule emailservice to a healthy node, with approval.
Watch checkoutservice latency (E1), which is likely a downstream effect, and confirm it recovers when emailservice does.
preconditions: Confirm emailservice has more than one healthy replica, or that a brief restart is acceptable, before any restart.
Verify the latency deviation is still ongoing (E3) so the action targets a live problem.
Record current deployment/config state and pod placement so changes can be reverted.
Obtain on-call approval before any restart, cordon, or config change.
proposed_fix.rollback: Restore the previous config or deployment revision (e.g. kubectl rollout undo), uncordon the node, and re-enable any removed rule; a restarted pod needs no rollback beyond confirming it is healthy.

contradictions.step: Check if CPU resource requests are adjusted to the app usage / Review existing quota for given namespace and adjust it accordingly. / Add more nodes to the cluster
contradictions.why: Emailservice's own span self-time is flat (0.19->0.19ms, 1.04x) with no errors, which does not point to CPU quota or capacity starvation, so quota and node-scaling steps are omitted.
contradictions.note: step not found in R4's text; check the runbook itself

contradictions.step: Investigate networking issues on the node... Replace physical cable / Increase TX queue length
contradictions.why: Only emailservice's inbound calls slowed, with no errors, rather than a node-wide receive-error pattern, so hardware and TX-queue changes are not supported and are omitted.
contradictions.note: step not found in R2's text; check the runbook itself

contradictions.step: Bump conntrack limit directly on the node, remembering to make it persistent across node reboots.
contradictions.why: No errors or drops appear in the traces, which gives no support for conntrack exhaustion, and a persistent node-level change is not a reversible first step.
